fact: There is an average of about 3 river-crossing deaths each year in NZ outdoors; 80% of these accidents occur in flooded rivers or side-streams
context: NZ Mountain Safety Council RIVER SAFETY document, opening statistics section
raw_quote: There is an average of about three river-crossing deaths each year. Eighty percent of these accidents occur in flooded rivers or side-streams. It's not only the inexperienced who die. Experienced and skilled people have drowned after being tempted to give it a go against their better judgement.

fact: MSC identifies 'get home-itis' as a significant factor in NZ river tragedies - trampers rush across creeks to reach hut/shelter after long day
context: MSC River Safety document, Roaring Stag Lodge (Eastern Tararuas) entry by Warren Granger, Manawatu
raw_quote: The main creek that leads to Ruamahanga River is very close to the hut – only 100m or so downstream – which can be very tempting to trampers who are anxious to retire to the hut immediately. Get home-itis has been a significant factor in river tragedies over the years.

fact: Named NZ tracks with recurring river-crossing incidents/drownings: Wilkin Valley (Kerrin Forks, Jumboland), Siberia to Lake Crucible, Young River mouth, East Matuki at Ruth Flat - all documented as sites of drownings, mainly in 'fresh' or 'flood' conditions
context: MSC River Safety document, Wanaka entry by Heather Thorne
raw_quote: River crossing is required at the following places: Wilkin Valley (Kerrin Forks and Jumboland), Siberia to Lake Crucible, the mouth of the Young River, and East Matuki at Ruth Flat. Drownings and incidents have occured at all of these crossings, mainly in 'fresh' or 'flood' conditions.

fact: Mt Tapuae-o-Uenuku (biggest peak north of Aoraki/Mt Cook) route requires 70+ river crossings; trampers can be trapped in Hodder Huts if river rises - only feasible route in/out
context: MSC River Safety document, Marlborough entry by Mark Anderson and Carol McKie
raw_quote: The trip up Mt Tapuae-o-Uenuku, the biggest peak north of Aoraki/Mt Cook, has more than 70 crossings. Trampers can easily be trapped in the Hodder Huts if the river rises, as it has a huge catchment and is the only feasible route to and from the mountain.

fact: Tongariro Alpine Crossing (NZ's most famous day hike, 20.2km): from early May to late October considered a difficult, expert-level trail with snow/ice covering trail, sub-freezing temps, avalanche risk. Guided hike strongly recommended in winter
context: visitruapehu.com Tongariro Alpine Crossing FAQ, 'best time' section
raw_quote: However from early May to late October, the Tongariro Alpine Crossing is considered a difficult, expert-level trail, and we strongly recommend a guided hike. During these winter months snow and ice can cover the trail, temperatures are frequently below freezing, and there is a risk of avalanches.

fact: DOC introduced mandatory booking system for Tongariro Alpine Crossing from 14 October 2023 for 2023/2024 season - due to overcrowding + environmental impact + safety issues from over-visitation
context: newzealand.com Tongariro National Park page, 'Important updates for visitors'
raw_quote: DOC introduced a booking system for the 2023/2024 season, where visitors using any part of the track should reserve slots in advance. Bookings are strongly encouraged and are required for booking a shuttle or guided walk. The booking system is now live for bookings 14 October 2023 onwards.

fact: Tongariro Alpine Crossing terrain: starts 1,120m elevation, ascends to 1,886m Red Crater, descends to 760m - net gain 766m, gross gain >1000m. 7-8 hours typical
context: visitruapehu.com Tongariro Alpine Crossing Elevation FAQ
raw_quote: The Tongariro Alpine Crossing has a starting elevation of 1,120 meters above sea level, ascending to an altitude of 1,886 meters at the Red Crater. The track descends to finish at 760 meters.

fact: Tongariro's Red Crater is still active - 'The sulphurous odour... is a reminder that this crater is still active'. Ngauruhoe last erupted 1975, Ruapehu last erupted 1996 - visitors must check current volcanic activity before hiking
context: newzealand.com Tongariro National Park page
raw_quote: Ruapehu and Tongariro, which date back before the last ice age, are two of the most active composite volcanoes in the world, with Ruapehu last erupting in 1996. Ngauruhoe – geologically considered a 'vent' – last erupted in 1975. Before you venture into Tongariro National Park it's essential to check the current volcanic activity.

fact: Tongariro Alpine Crossing between May-Oct requires alpine skills; the Round the Mountain track (Ruapehu, 66km, 6 days) between June-Aug requires 'alpine equipment and navigation skills essential' due to snow/ice - explicitly not suitable for average hikers in winter
context: newzealand.com Tongariro National Park page, Round the Mountain section
raw_quote: In winter (June to August) this track should only be attempted by experienced, well-equipped hikers. During this time, snow and ice are common, making alpine equipment and navigation skills essential.
